purpose: Research registry for testing-facility design pressure. Titles only; no direct external URLs are stored in the cube.

sources.title: Bazel Test Encyclopedia
sources.take: Define the test environment and expected runner behavior explicitly; BrowserRT should make its test environment a contract.

sources.title: Bazel common definitions for test size and timeout
sources.take: Small/medium/large style sizing and default timeouts support early classification of test cost.

sources.title: Google Testing Blog test sizes
sources.take: Small/medium/large language is useful, but BrowserRT adds micro and determinism classes for cloudtainer turns.

sources.title: Google Testing Blog flaky tests by size
sources.take: Large tests are more likely to be flaky; BrowserRT should keep browser/GPU/mesh checks sliced.

sources.title: Playwright parallelism documentation
sources.take: Worker processes speed suites but require resource isolation and no shared state assumptions.

sources.title: Playwright sharding documentation
sources.take: Sharding is a first-class way to split large suites; BrowserRT implements deterministic weighted shards early.

sources.title: Node.js test runner documentation
sources.take: Node has a built-in baseline with setup/reporting concepts; BrowserRT keeps a custom zero-dependency harness for manifest economics.

sources.title: Vitest performance documentation
sources.take: Parallelism can have overhead; BrowserRT caps jobs and requires serial groups for shared resources.

sources.title: pytest-xdist documentation
sources.take: Distributed and parallel test execution must respect isolation boundaries; BrowserRT captures serial groups and lane ownership early.

sources.title: Nx affected documentation
sources.take: Run only tasks affected by changed surfaces when possible; BrowserRT adds --changed based on manifest inputs.

sources.title: Nx distributed task execution and timing distribution
sources.take: Average runtime based assignment reduces idle time; BrowserRT timing history can feed shard weights.

sources.title: Turborepo remote caching documentation
sources.take: Avoid duplicated work by fingerprinting inputs and outputs; BrowserRT can imitate locally without remote services.

sources.title: Turborepo remote caching documentation
sources.take: Shared cache is powerful but out of scope for cloudtainer-only; local cache design must remain self-contained.

sources.title: Chrome DevTools Protocol documentation
sources.take: CDP is the control plane for local browser instrumentation, inspection, debugging, profiling, and future harness work.

sources.title: Chrome Developers headless Chrome article
sources.take: Headless browsers are appropriate for automated tests and server-like environments; BrowserRT should start one only inside a scoped command.

sources.title: MDN PerformanceLongTaskTiming
sources.take: Long task entries expose UI-thread tasks at or above the long-task threshold; BrowserRT can use them as jank signals.

sources.title: MDN PerformanceObserver
sources.take: PerformanceObserver streams performance entries while a page runs; future browser tests should collect these traces.

sources.title: Web Platform Tests documentation
sources.take: A large browser-facing conformance suite should inspire BrowserRT to make every browser proof path-addressable, subsettable, and harness-visible.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions
sources.take: Common attribute names help traces tell a coherent story; BrowserRT should define its own small conventions early.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry traces documentation
sources.take: Spans describe operations and relationships; BrowserRT traces can map task, worker, storage, GPU, and browser events.
